messages:
maria: Quick sync — putting together a hitlist of audit-log gaps across API-gateway, auth, console, billing, runtime. Need to map to RBAC changes + KMS key events + what customers require for compliance. Who has the latest gaps?

tom: I can start — I ran a quick pass against the schema checklist. Short list: API gateway missing proxy-level route-authorize events, runtime missing container-image-change events, billing missing invoice-access event for support users.

laura: console: we still don't emit `admin_role_grant` with the previous_role and approver fields. Customers ask for approver/req_id for SOX proof. Also UI action -> backend translation sometimes drops the trace_id.

kevin: KMS questions: when keys rotate, do we log the key alias + rotation reason + who triggered it? Are we ok including key_id/alias in cleartext in audit events? legal/security worried about key identifiers being linkable to key usage metadata.

maria: good Q — we must never log key material. key alias/id is OK if we treat it like metadata (no plaintext key material). We should tag key events with event_type: key.rotate/key.create/key.disable and actor. We need a short schema for customer-facing events — keep it minimal.

sam: fwiw, billing: support agents using impersonation don't create an `impersonation_start` event currently. That stops us proving who accessed invoices.

tom: runtime: for rollout hooks we don't surface what image digest was used in the audit event — only the service name. need digest + image.registry.

kevin: also, for RBAC changes, we should capture delta set rather than whole policy blobs. i.e. event.payload: {added:["role_x"], removed:["role_y"]} so diffs are compact and don't leak old policy snapshots.

maria: agree. propose a tiny JSON example to standardize on for customer-facing audit events (PII-redacted):

```
{
  "event_ts": "2024-06-17T15:12:03Z",
  "service": "console",
  "actor": "alice@example.com",
  "event_type": "admin_role_grant",
  "resource": "org:acme",
  "payload": {
    "role_added": ["billing_admin"],
    "previous_roles": ["viewer"],
    "approver": "bob@example.com",
    "req_id": "req_01F..."
  },
  "trace_id": "t-12345",
  "notes": "customer-visible"
}
```

kevin: that looks fine. for KMS rotate events swap `payload` to include `key_alias` and `rotation_reason` but not material. e.g. `payload:{"key_alias":"rwd-prod-1","rotation_reason":"scheduled","triggered_by":"ops@"}`

laura: does everyone agree we should version the audit schema (audit_v) so we can roll out changes and consumers can fallback?

maria: yes — include `audit_schema_version` at top-level. We'll do semver-like major bump when breaking. Also need a migration plan for internal consumers and support docs for customers.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: staging alert — missing `impersonation_start` events for billing in staging as of 1718642200.

tom: i'll take billing impersonation and console approver fields this sprint. ETA EOD Thursday.

kevin: i'll scope KMS rotation events + policy-diff payload for RBAC. will open PR with schema draft and unit tests.

sam: runtime image-digest events -> I'll add image.digest and registry to the deploy hook emitter. quick test on canary then roll.

maria: super. Action items: 1) tom - billing impersonation + console approver (1718645600) 2) kevin - kms + rbac-diff schema (1718722000) 3) sam - runtime image digest (1718700000) 4) laura - write customer-facing validation doc and examples (1718750000). I'll collate schema PRs and propose `audit_schema_version: 2.0` for initial rollout.

laura: I'll also add a short checklist for what to include/exclude in customer-facing events (no secrets, no full policy blobs, redacted user ids as optional).

maria: thanks all — ping me if blockers. we should present this at next compliance review. :thumbsup:
